target.title: fix(memory-core): clear pending-update wait timer after update settles
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `memory_search` calls during an in-flight QMD reindex would each leak a ref'd 500ms timer. `QmdMemoryManager.waitForPendingUpdateBeforeSearch` races the pending reindex update against a `setTimeout`-based 500ms bound; when the pending update resolved first (the common case - reindex completes in under 500ms), the timeout was never cleared, so each search left a pending timer. Sustained `memory_search` traffic during a reindex stacked pending timers, each holding event-loop interest until it fired.

## Why This Change Was Made

The wait helper now captures the `setTimeout` handle and clears it in a `finally` when the pending update settles first, following the same `try/finally + clearTimeout` convention already used by the sibling memory-core wait helpers (`manager-embedding-ops.ts`, `tools.ts`) and by `packages/ai/src/internal/retry-sleep.ts`, whose comment documents the identical leak class: "Successful retry waits must detach from the run-level signal; otherwise every retry retains this promise closure until the whole run aborts." The method's contract is unchanged - it still waits up to 500ms for a pending update to settle before proceeding - and the change is bounded to the one leaf method. No new helper is introduced; the inline `try/finally + clearTimeout` matches the local convention.

## User Impact

**Before:** each `memory_search` during an active reindex left a pending 500ms timer when the reindex finished quickly, and repeated searches stacked them.

**After:** the wait timer is cleared as soon as the pending update settles. The fast path (search proceeds immediately) and the full-500ms-wait path are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Stock pinned main (`08843c74de`) retained 50 pending `Timeout` handles after 50 production wait calls where the pending update resolved first; each was the 500ms wait timeout, left pending because the operation arm won the race without clearing it.
- Current-head production timer-lifecycle proof used the real `QmdMemoryManager.waitForPendingUpdateBeforeSearch()` method with real Node timers and `process.getActiveResourcesInfo()`:

  ```text
  BEFORE 08843c74de (origin/main)
  iterations=50
  pendingResolvedQuickly=true
  baselineTimeouts=0
  afterTimeouts=50
  leakedTimeouts=50

  AFTER fix
  iterations=50
  pendingResolvedQuickly=true
  baselineTimeouts=0
  afterTimeouts=0
  leakedTimeouts=0
  ```

  The uncommitted harness imported the real `QmdMemoryManager` class, created a real instance carrying the real prototype method (the method reads only `this.pendingUpdate`; the full `create()` factory spawns the external qmd process, which is out of scope for this timer-lifecycle proof), set `pendingUpdate` to an already-resolved `Promise` (reindex completed in under 500ms, the common case), and counted actual pending `Timeout` handles via Node's `process.getActiveResourcesInfo()`. Both runs were reproducible across two executions each.
- Committed regression guard (`qmd-manager.timer-leak.test.ts`): 1 file passed, 1 test passed. Uses real timers and `process.getActiveResourcesInfo()` (no fake timers, no mock assertions); verified to fail on the base (positive delta) and pass on the fix.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/memory-core/src/memory/qmd-manager.test.ts` -> 8 failed | 141 passed on base; 8 failed | 145 passed on fix. The 8 failures are pre-existing SQLite store-writer-queue failures, identical on `origin/main` and unrelated to this timer change; zero new failures introduced.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxlint --threads=1 extensions/memory-core/src/memory/qmd-manager.ts extensions/memory-core/src/memory/qmd-manager.timer-leak.test.ts`
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/memory-core/src/memory/qmd-manager.ts extensions/memory-core/src/memory/qmd-manager.timer-leak.test.ts`
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`

Impact-surface review traced `pendingUpdate` from its set site (`this.pendingUpdate = run().finally(() => { this.pendingUpdate = null; })`) through `waitForPendingUpdateBeforeSearch` and its single caller in `search()`, and checked sibling memory-core wait helpers (all already clear their timers on settle). A fresh open-PR search found no PR covering this timer leak.

Fix classification: root cause fix. No schema, default, migration, protocol, or provider behavior changes.
